# JSON

> A JSON editor that runs in the browser, at https://json.frameworkphp.com.ar/.
> A link can carry a document, so opening it shows the document right away,
> as a tree, as a table or as text, and two of them compared.

The document goes after the `#` of the link, which the browser never sends
anywhere. There are two ways to write it.

## Written out

For a short document. The value is percent-encoded, the way
`encodeURIComponent` in JavaScript and `urllib.parse.quote(text, safe="")` in
Python do it: a space is `%20`, a new line is `%0A`, and a `+` stays a plus.

    https://json.frameworkphp.com.ar/#json=<text>

## Packed

For anything longer. The fields go in a JSON object, which is gzipped and
written in base64, in either alphabet, with or without the padding.

    https://json.frameworkphp.com.ar/#z=<base64 of the gzip of the JSON>

In Python:

    import base64, gzip, json
    fields = { "json": document, "name": "result.json", "mode": "tree" }
    packed = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(gzip.compress(json.dumps(fields).encode())).decode()
    print("https://json.frameworkphp.com.ar/#z=" + packed)

In a shell, with the document on disk:

    jq -n --slurpfile doc result.json '{json: $doc[0], name: "result.json"}' \
        | gzip -9 | base64 | tr -d '\n' \
        | sed 's|^|https://json.frameworkphp.com.ar/#z=|'

## Fields

- `json`: the document. In a packed link it is either the JSON itself or its
  text; written out it is always the text. A text that is not valid JSON is
  shown as it is, with where it stops being JSON.
- `name`: optional, the name of the document.
- `mode`: optional, one of `tree` (the default), `table` (for a list of
  objects) or `text`.
- `right`, `rightName`: optional, a second document, shown beside the first.
- `compare`: optional, `true` to mark where the two documents differ.

## Showing it

Give the link as a Markdown link, since the address is long. When you run on
the machine of whoever is to see the document, open it for them instead, which
has no chat in the way to cut a long address short:

    open "<link>"          # macOS
    xdg-open "<link>"      # Linux
